decisions.evidence: R1 maker baseline: 'Saving, viewing, editing...' with client noting 'Right now it reads like I'm required to type the title, and the notes even say pulling that info automatically isn't part of this.' R1 client: 'if I just paste in a web address, the app goes and grabs the page's name, a short description, and its little icon for me — I can tweak it after'.
decisions.note: Spec-review gate. Baseline required manual title entry and explicitly excluded auto-collection, contradicting REF-BM-02 (auto title/description/favicon/preview) and REF-BM-03 (editable). Client rejects the mismatch and supplies the conforming behaviour. Preview-image sub-part not individually named but auto-metadata+editable substantially corrected.

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'A "read it later" idea... I'd like to flag those and see just that list, then check them off once I've read them.' Absent from R1 baseline presentation; R2 maker adds 'A read-later queue with read/unread status'.
decisions.note: Spec review. Read-later queue, separate unread view, and mark-read were absent from presented scope; client requests the missing reference requirements → extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'Being able to tuck a bookmark away without deleting it... out of my normal list, but I can still get it back later. Deleting feels too final.' R2 maker adds 'Reversible archive and restore'.
decisions.note: Spec review. Reversible archive distinct from permanent delete was absent from baseline; client requests it → extend (REF-BM-26 hide-from-default, REF-BM-27 archive-vs-delete distinction).

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'Sorting my list — at least by name or by when I added it. You've listed sorting as out of scope, but I'd want basic control over the order.' R2 maker: 'Sorting by title or date in either direction'.
decisions.note: Spec review. Baseline explicitly placed sorting out of scope, contradicting REF-BM-22; client rejects the exclusion and supplies the conforming sort keys → correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 client: 'Search that's a bit smarter than plain word matching — like searching an exact phrase, or combining a couple of tags to narrow things down.' R2 maker: 'Exact-phrase search and combined tag/state filters'.
decisions.note: Spec review. Baseline search was plain word matching only; client requests exact-phrase (REF-BM-16) and multi-tag narrowing (beyond single-tag REF-BM-11) → extend. Full boolean operators tracked separately.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker presented search as 'Exact-phrase search and combined tag/state filters'; no AND/OR/NOT/parentheses/quoting rule or #tag syntax. Client (R1/R2) expressed only exact-phrase and 'combining a couple of tags', never boolean operators or #tag search.
decisions.note: Spec review. The presented search feature diverges from REF-BM-15 (boolean operators, parentheses, operator-quoting rule) and REF-BM-14 (#tag syntax); this difference passed without any client expression → unexpressed. Weakest inference but the search decision was presented.

decisions.evidence: R1 baseline listed 'Clear exclusions for... imports/exports'. R1 client: 'being able to bring in the bookmarks I already have (and get them back out)... let me know your thinking on... importing?' R2 maker adds 'Imports from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari... Complete export'; R2 client: 'bring my existing bookmarks in and get my whole collection back out gives me peace of mind.'
decisions.note: Spec review. Baseline explicitly excluded import/export contradicting REF-BM-30/31; client raised it (pending at R1) and requested inclusion, resolved conforming at R2. Linked clarification→disposition counted once as corrective.

decisions.evidence: R1 client (pending): 'keeping my own saved copy of a page so I don't lose it if the site disappears... I'd at least want us to talk about rather than rule out flat.' R2 maker defers snapshots. R2 client accepts: 'I'm fine with your plan. You're not throwing it away, just handling it properly on its own later... I'd like to keep it on the list as a real "next" thing.' Reaffirmed R5.
decisions.note: Spec review. Page snapshot (REF-BM-24) and Internet Archive (REF-BM-25) deferred = departure from reference. Client explicitly states the expectation and identifies the difference (deferred not included) and accepts without requesting alignment → accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. R1 expression recorded as pending, resolved R2; not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: R2 client: 'when I add a tag... as I start typing it suggests tags I've already used, so I don't accidentally make a slightly different duplicate... just wanted to make sure that little as-you-type help is there.' R3 maker: 'The tag suggestion behavior is explicitly included in the approved specification.'
decisions.note: Spec review. Tag autocomplete was not present in rounds 1-2 presentations; client raised the reference requirement (REF-BM-10) and it was confirmed included at R3. Client's own explicit expression of the as-you-type expectation → corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker baseline lists 'Duplicate-link prevention'. R5 client confirms: 'Trying to save something I already have stops me and points me at the one I've got — even when I typed it in a slightly different way, like different capitalization or an extra slash.'
decisions.note: Recorded conforming decision matching REF-BM-06 (re-saving existing url guides to the existing bookmark). Present from baseline; no divergence.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker baseline: 'Saving, viewing, editing, favoriting, tagging, and deleting bookmarks'. Confirmed across R2-R5 client approvals.
decisions.note: Bundled recorded conforming core CRUD/list/tag decisions (REF-BM-01 save, REF-BM-04 edit, REF-BM-05 delete, REF-BM-07 list, REF-BM-09 tags). Favoriting is an extra non-reference feature, not judged. No divergence.
